focus: Final sweep before the depth checkpoint: hooks and runtime wiring — git hook scripts, the hook installer, .claude/.codex/.opencode hook configs; find an exit-0-on-failure hook, a config-named hook missing on disk, or an unread documented env switch; re-run the strongest check-mode repros.
answeredQuestions: What friction do the operator and the AI user hit in doctor output, hook rejections and CI failures?

graphEvents.label: Friction in doctor output, hook rejections and CI failures
Installer --status reports every hook SHADOWED through the .opencode alias
Global core.hooksPath makes this checkout load-bearing machine-wide
pre-commit test sets SPECKIT_SKIP_DOC_MODEL_VALIDATE that no hook reads

label: install-git-hooks.sh --status reports all 7 hooks as SHADOWED when the installed link reaches the same file through the .opencode/scripts -> ../.skilled/scripts alias; resolve_target follows one symlink hop without canonicalising and the check compares strings, so the message 'resolves outside this checkout' is false. doctor-git-hooks.yaml:82 then instructs the agent to tell the operator their hooks run another checkout's copy.

install-git-hooks.sh --status ends in an unconditional exit 0, so a genuinely absent hook prints '(not installed)' as prose and the command still succeeds; the one command the doctor workflow tells the agent to run carries no machine signal. check-git-hooks.sh already uses the better pattern of warning to stderr and documenting the advisory contract.
verify: bash .skilled/scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --status >/dev/null; echo $?  # 0 even with a hook missing

label: A global core.hooksPath pointing into this checkout makes this working tree load-bearing for commit and push gates in every repository on the machine; the installer warns only about the linked-worktree dangling-symlink variant it did not create, and nothing checks a global hooks dir whose links dangle after this checkout moves. Removing the global layer breaks nothing in this repo, so it is the removable layer.

pre-commit.test.sh:34 runs the hook with SPECKIT_SKIP_DOC_MODEL_VALIDATE=1, a name no hook or lib outside tests/ reads; pre-commit gates on SPECKIT_SKIP_DOC_VERSION_BUMP and four others instead, so the test asserts a skip it never gets and passes for a reason unrelated to its intent.

Every hook path named in .claude/settings.json (31 hook entries across PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, Stop, SessionEnd, PostToolUse, PreCompact) resolves on disk; .codex/settings.json and .opencode/settings.json do not exist, so the missing-file lead is closed for the Claude runtime.

The fail-open hypothesis on pre-commit is refuted: the hook-flags bootstrap prints 'commit gates remain enabled' on both a non-zero source and a missing lib, so it fails closed. The only silent exit is the operator's own kill switch, already recorded.

The 'doctor never reads core.hooksPath' hypothesis is refuted: git-hook-gates.cjs reads gates.tsv by design and git-setup-check.cjs:438 owns the hooks-path resolution. Only the installer's status rendering is wrong.

All 22 SKILLED_*/SPECKIT_* variables the hooks README documents are read by hook code; the drift is in the opposite direction, four undocumented reads, two of which are test-only and therefore not operator switches.
